name: What is the difference between a bump-out and a full kitchen addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a bump-out and a full kitchen addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out is a small extension of an existing room that does not require a new foundation, often cantilevered or supported by joists, typically adding only a few feet of space. It's a more modest way to gain space or light. A full kitchen addition, however, involves constructing a new foundation and expanding the kitchen significantly, adding substantial square footage and often reconfiguring the entire layout. Full additions offer greater design flexibility and space.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out is a small extension without a new foundation, while a full kitchen addition involves a new foundation and significantly expands the kitchen's square footage.
